meta.name: Frontend Product Builder Analytical Data Components
meta.description: Canonical components for metric hierarchy, normalized statuses, temporal history, and data-freshness communication.

MetricCard.name: MetricCard
MetricCard.description: Canonical presentation for one decision-relevant metric, including value, unit, comparison, trend meaning, status, freshness, and an optional contextual action.
capabilities: Present one metric with explicit semantic priority.
Separate the current value from comparison, trend, status, and freshness context.
Communicate zero, unavailable, partial, stale, loading, and error states.
Distinguish numerical movement from whether that movement is favorable or unfavorable.
Expose a low-frequency contextual action without turning the complete card into an ambiguous control.

foundation.reason: Metric presentation requires strict semantic hierarchy, state distinction, trend interpretation, freshness context, responsive behavior, and consistent content anatomy beyond a generic card.

primary.intent: Present a dominant metric directly connected to the principal decision or operational objective of the current screen.
allowedUse: One or two highest-priority dashboard metrics.
Metric that determines immediate user attention.
prohibitedUse: Metric with no clear user decision attached.

supporting.intent: Present a secondary metric that helps explain or qualify a primary metric.
allowedUse: Metric used to explain a dominant result.
prohibitedUse: Primary metric disguised as lower priority.

attention.intent: Present a metric whose current state requires operational attention.
prohibitedUse: Metrics that are healthy or neutral.
Using danger tone only to make a card more visible.

progress.intent: Present progress toward a defined target using authoritative current and target values.
prohibitedUse: Long-running operation status better represented by ProcessingState.

comparison.intent: Present a current metric whose primary purpose is comparison with another period, segment, target, or baseline.
prohibitedUse: Misleading percentage change from a zero or unavailable baseline.

compact.intent: Dense metric inside a constrained panel or supporting dashboard region.

large.intent: Dominant decision metric with additional supporting context.

slots.name: label
slots.description: Concise user-facing name of the metric.
contentRestrictions: Use user-oriented terminology rather than raw field names.
The label must make the metric understandable without relying only on an icon.

slots.name: context
slots.description: Optional scope, period, segment, or qualification of the metric.
contentRestrictions: Name the period, scope, or population when ambiguity is possible.
Do not hide the baseline only in a tooltip.

slots.name: value
slots.description: Primary formatted metric value.
contentRestrictions: The value must already follow approved locale and domain formatting.
Zero, unavailable, and not calculated must remain distinct.
Do not render raw floating-point precision.

slots.name: unit
slots.description: Optional unit, currency, percentage, duration, or count qualifier.
contentRestrictions: The unit must not contradict the formatted value.
Currency and percentage formatting follow project locale policy.

slots.name: comparison
slots.description: Optional named baseline, target, previous period, or benchmark.
contentRestrictions: The comparison baseline must be named.
Do not show percentage change when the baseline makes the calculation misleading.

slots.name: trend
slots.description: Optional movement direction and semantic interpretation.
contentRestrictions: Direction and favorability are separate concepts.
An upward trend must not automatically use success semantics.
Trend requires a defined comparison interval.

slots.name: status
slots.description: Optional normalized operational status.
contentRestrictions: Status must not duplicate the same meaning already communicated through the label and value.
Critical explanatory content requires InlineAlert rather than a badge alone.

slots.name: supporting
slots.description: Optional concise explanation, target, numerator, denominator, or data-quality context.
contentRestrictions: Keep the content concise.
Detailed analysis belongs in the analytical region below.

slots.name: freshness
slots.description: Optional indication of when the metric was last calculated or synchronized.
contentRestrictions: Required when the metric is not real-time and decision quality depends on recency.

slots.name: action
slots.description: Optional low-frequency action such as opening the underlying collection or explanation.
contentRestrictions: Do not make the entire card clickable when the interaction would be ambiguous.
The action label must explain its destination or result.

props.name: variant
props.description: Semantic role of the metric in the current information hierarchy.
restrictions: Variant selection must follow the screen contract and metric hierarchy.
Do not use primary for every metric.

props.name: size
props.description: Metric density and visual scale.
restrictions: Large is reserved for dominant metrics.

props.name: trendDirection
props.description: Numerical movement relative to an explicitly named baseline.
restrictions: Direction does not determine whether the movement is good or bad.

props.name: trendMeaning
props.description: Domain interpretation of the current movement.
restrictions: The owning feature resolves the domain meaning.
The shared component does not infer meaning from direction.

props.name: loading
props.description: Indicates initial metric loading when no authoritative value exists.
restrictions: Background refresh preserves the current value.

props.name: refreshing
props.description: Indicates non-blocking synchronization while the current metric remains visible.
restrictions: Refreshing must not replace the value with a skeleton.

spacingOwnership: MetricCard owns spacing among label, context, value, unit, comparison, trend, status, supporting content, freshness, and action.
MetricGroup owns spacing among peer MetricCard instances.
The containing section owns spacing around the metric group.
composition.surfaceOwnership: MetricCard owns one metric surface. It must not add decorative nested cards around comparison, trend, or freshness content.
rules: One card represents one coherent metric.
Metric priority is explicit.
Zero is not treated as unavailable.
Trend direction and trend meaning remain separate.
A card is not automatically interactive.
Metric state is supplied by the owning feature or query.

recipeCompatibility.notes: Primary, supporting, and attention metrics require explicit hierarchy.
Use only for decision-relevant entity metrics, not ordinary attributes.
Use for operational health or configured-resource summaries.
Confidence, evidence count, or risk metrics require clear provenance and must not replace human judgment.
Use sparingly for collection-level summary metrics.

notes: The owning feature supplies formatted values, normalized states, comparison context, trend meaning, and callbacks.
Optional actions receive explicit callbacks from the owning feature.

responsive.strategy: Preserve label, value, operational meaning, and freshness while moving low-priority context below the value.
responsive.compact: Use compact padding, wrap the label, keep the value readable, and stack comparison, status, freshness, and action.
responsive.medium: Use default metric composition with wrapping supporting context.
responsive.wide: Allow horizontal alignment of comparison, trend, freshness, and low-frequency action when readable.
responsive.ultrawide: The card does not expand its typography or add low-value content merely to fill width.
responsive.overflowPolicy: Values, labels, and metadata wrap or use approved numeric formatting. No page-level horizontal overflow.
responsive.zoomExpectation: Supporting regions stack before the primary value or action becomes unreadable at 125% browser zoom.

accessibility.semanticElement: article or section when the metric is independently meaningful; otherwise a grouped neutral container
keyboard: Static metric content is not focusable.
Optional actions and disclosures are keyboard operable.
focus: Interactive metric actions follow the complete readable metric content.
Background refresh does not reset focus.
announcements: Initial loading and error are announced through canonical feedback behavior.
Routine metric refreshes are not repeatedly announced.
Material status changes may be announced by StatusBadge or the owning workflow.
aria: Do not use meter or progress semantics unless the metric actually represents a bounded target.
Trend icons are decorative when the textual trend meaning is already present.
Icon-only actions require explicit accessible names.
accessibility.colorIndependence: Trend meaning, attention state, progress, stale state, and status use text, semantics, icons, or labels in addition to color.

content.minimum: A user-facing label and one authoritative value or canonical unavailable state.
content.typical: Label, scope, value, unit, comparison or trend, and freshness.
content.maximum: One metric with concise supporting context; detailed analysis belongs in another region.
content.wrapping: Labels, comparison, trend explanation, freshness, and actions wrap naturally.
content.truncation: Primary metric labels and values must not be truncated into ambiguity.
content.localization: Support localized numbers, currencies, percentages, durations, dates, and expanded labels.
content.emptyBehavior: A metric without an authoritative value uses a deliberate unavailable, not calculated, restricted, loading, or error state.
content.technicalContent: Raw query names, database aggregations, internal metric keys, and unformatted floating-point values are prohibited.

notes: A feature-level metric adapter may calculate and format domain values but must compose the canonical MetricCard.
MetricCard does not replace charts, tables, or detailed analytical explanations.

MetricGroup.name: MetricGroup
MetricGroup.description: Canonical metric composition that establishes hierarchy, grouping, comparison relationships, responsive layout, and state ownership across several MetricCard instances.
capabilities: Arrange several related metrics according to explicit semantic priority.
Separate dominant metrics from supporting metrics.
Define whether metrics are hierarchical, balanced, comparative, or compact.
Prevent indiscriminate equal-card dashboards.
Transform metric layouts according to content and available width.
Represent group-level loading, failure, emptiness, permission, and freshness context.

foundation.reason: Metric collections require semantic hierarchy, bounded density, responsive transformation, state composition, and comparison rules beyond a generic grid.

hierarchical.intent: Present one or two dominant metrics followed by supporting metrics with lower visual weight.
prohibitedUse: Direct side-by-side comparison requiring equal visual weight.

balanced.intent: Present a small set of genuinely peer metrics with equal informational importance.
allowedUse: Three or four equivalent operational dimensions.
prohibitedUse: A group containing one clearly dominant metric.
Using equal cards only for visual symmetry.

comparison.intent: Present metrics whose primary relationship is direct comparison across segments, periods, states, or scenarios.
prohibitedUse: Metrics without a shared unit or meaningful comparison contract.
Unrelated metrics forced into one group.

compact.intent: Present a bounded set of short supporting metrics in a constrained region.
prohibitedUse: More metrics than can be scanned clearly.

compact.intent: Reduced metric-group spacing inside a constrained region.

default.intent: Ordinary dashboard and analytical metric grouping.

slots.name: heading
slots.description: Optional heading naming the coherent metric group.
contentRestrictions: Use when the group is not already named by the containing section.
Do not repeat the route title.

slots.name: description
slots.description: Optional concise explanation of scope, period, or decision purpose.
contentRestrictions: Name the reporting period or scope when needed.
Do not place lengthy analytical interpretation here.

slots.name: primaryMetrics
slots.description: Dominant metrics requiring the highest information priority.
contentRestrictions: Hierarchical mode normally permits one or two primary metrics.
Primary metrics must support the main decision or task.

slots.name: supportingMetrics
slots.description: Secondary metrics that explain, qualify, or supplement the primary metrics.
contentRestrictions: Supporting metrics must belong to the same analytical question.
Do not include unrelated KPIs merely to fill the grid.

slots.name: context
slots.description: Optional shared scope, comparison baseline, freshness, or data-quality context.
contentRestrictions: Shared context should not be repeated identically inside every MetricCard.

slots.name: state
slots.description: Group-level loading, error, empty, permission, unavailable, or stale state.
contentRestrictions: Render the state at the smallest truthful scope.
One failed supporting metric should not automatically replace the complete group.

slots.name: action
slots.description: Optional group-level action such as opening the full analytical route.
contentRestrictions: Do not duplicate actions already present in each metric.
The action remains secondary to the metric content.

props.name: variant
props.description: Semantic relationship among the metrics.
restrictions: Do not select balanced merely to obtain equal card widths.
Comparison mode requires a shared comparison contract.

props.name: size
props.description: Approved group density.
restrictions: Compact does not justify overcrowding.

props.name: loading
props.description: Indicates that no authoritative group metrics are yet available.
restrictions: When some metrics are available, render partial state at the metric level when possible.

props.name: refreshing
props.description: Indicates background synchronization while current metrics remain visible.
restrictions: Refreshing does not replace populated metrics with skeletons.

spacingOwnership: MetricGroup owns gaps and responsive placement among primary and supporting metrics.
Each MetricCard owns its internal spacing.
The containing section owns spacing around the complete metric group.
composition.surfaceOwnership: MetricGroup owns no additional outer card by default. MetricCard instances own their own metric surfaces.
rules: Metrics require a coherent analytical relationship.
Primary and supporting metrics remain explicitly separated.
The number of metrics is bounded by scanability and decision relevance.
MetricGroup is not a generic card grid.
Group-level states render only when they truthfully affect the group.

recipeCompatibility.notes: The dashboard contract must define which metrics are primary, supporting, and attention-oriented.
Use only when several decision-relevant entity metrics form a coherent group.
Use for bounded operational-health and configuration summaries.
Use a compact bounded group rather than a full dashboard.
Metrics must not imply automated decision authority.

notes: The screen or feature supplies metric hierarchy, data states, shared context, and actions.
Optional group-level actions are supplied externally.

responsive.strategy: Collapse hierarchy into a readable vertical sequence while preserving primary metrics before supporting metrics.
responsive.compact: Primary metrics render first and full width. Supporting metrics follow in one column or an approved compact two-column arrangement.
responsive.medium: Primary metrics retain dominant width; supporting metrics use one or two columns according to minimum readable width.
responsive.wide: Use the selected hierarchical, balanced, comparison, or compact layout.
responsive.ultrawide: Do not increase metric count or typography merely because more width exists.
responsive.overflowPolicy: Metrics wrap into additional rows. Horizontal page overflow is prohibited.
responsive.zoomExpectation: The group collapses columns before metric labels, values, or actions become unreadable at 125% browser zoom.

accessibility.semanticElement: section or grouped list of independently labeled metric articles
accessibility.accessibleName: Visible group heading or accessible label supplied by the containing section.
keyboard: Metric and group actions remain keyboard operable.
focus: DOM order follows primary metrics before supporting metrics.
Responsive layout must not reorder metric meaning through CSS alone.
announcements: Group-level loading and errors use canonical feedback announcements.
Routine metric refreshes do not produce repeated live announcements.
aria: Use semantic grouping rather than ARIA grid.
Each independently meaningful metric retains an accessible label.
accessibility.colorIndependence: Metric hierarchy is conveyed through structure, typography, labels, and order rather than color alone.

content.minimum: One primary or supporting MetricCard inside a named analytical context.
content.typical: One or two primary metrics and two to six supporting metrics.
content.maximum: A bounded set that remains scannable and decision-relevant; large metric inventories require prioritization or another route.
content.wrapping: Cards wrap by semantic group and minimum readable width.
content.truncation: Metric labels and values must not be truncated into ambiguity.
content.localization: Support expanded labels, values, comparison text, dates, and actions.
content.emptyBehavior: An empty group does not render unless it presents an explicit EmptyState.
content.technicalContent: Raw metric keys, database aggregation names, model feature names, and internal calculation identifiers are prohibited.

notes: MetricGroup does not choose metrics or priorities. These decisions belong to product and screen contracts.
Equal visual treatment requires genuine informational equivalence.

StatusBadge.name: StatusBadge
StatusBadge.description: Canonical normalized status presentation that maps an approved semantic state into a concise label, icon, tone, and accessible meaning.
capabilities: Present a concise normalized status.
Communicate neutral, informational, successful, warning, dangerous, processing, stale, and unavailable states.
Separate domain status mapping from visual tone.
Provide accessible text and optional supporting context.
Prevent each feature from inventing independent status colors and labels.

foundation.reason: StatusBadge constrains domain adapters to normalized semantic states while centralizing labels, icons, accessible meaning, tone, and compact presentation.

neutral.intent: Communicate an ordinary, inactive, draft, unknown-neutral, or categorically neutral state.

info.intent: Communicate an informational state without positive or negative outcome.

success.intent: Communicate backend-confirmed completion, health, activation, or successful outcome.
allowedUse: Approved by an authoritative human or policy.
prohibitedUse: Optimistic assumption not confirmed by the backend.

warning.intent: Communicate a state requiring attention or caution without confirmed failure.

danger.intent: Communicate failure, blocking state, expiration, critical risk, or rejected outcome.

processing.intent: Communicate an operation that is queued, running, synchronizing, or awaiting completion.
prohibitedUse: Initial data loading without a domain operation.

stale.intent: Communicate that the represented information or result is outdated, superseded, or requires refresh.
prohibitedUse: Blocking conflict that needs a full StaleDataNotice.

unavailable.intent: Communicate that a status cannot currently be determined or presented.
prohibitedUse: Permission-restricted status whose existence must not be disclosed.

compact.intent: Dense status label for tables, metadata, and compact headers.

default.intent: Prominent status in entity orientation, review, and analytical summaries.

slots.name: icon
slots.description: Optional icon matching the normalized semantic state.
contentRestrictions: The icon must match the semantic tone.
The icon must not be the only source of meaning.
Motion must respect reduced-motion preferences.

slots.name: label
slots.description: Concise localized status label.
contentRestrictions: Use user-facing terminology.
Do not display raw backend enum keys.
Avoid ambiguous labels such as OK when a precise state exists.

slots.name: context
slots.description: Optional accessible or visible context distinguishing similar states.
contentRestrictions: Critical context must remain visible rather than tooltip-only.
Tooltip context is supplementary.

props.name: tone
props.type: neutral | info | success | warning | danger | processing | stale | unavailable
props.description: Normalized semantic presentation tone.
restrictions: The owning domain adapter maps raw status values into this normalized tone.
Do not select a tone only to obtain a desired color.

props.name: size
props.description: Approved status-label scale.
restrictions: Large custom status pills are prohibited.

props.name: animated
props.description: Allows approved subtle motion for an active processing state.
restrictions: Allowed only for processing.
Must respect reduced-motion preferences.
Motion must not be the only evidence that processing continues.

prohibitedParents: Button when the status is only decorative
Tooltip as the only status label
spacingOwnership: StatusBadge owns spacing between icon, label, and optional context.
The containing component owns spacing around the complete badge.
composition.surfaceOwnership: StatusBadge owns one compact semantic status surface.
rules: Raw domain status mapping occurs outside the shared component.
Status labels are localized and user-facing.
Success requires authoritative confirmation.
Complex blocking states require a larger feedback component.
The component is non-interactive by default.

recipeCompatibility.notes: Use normalized status labels rather than feature-specific colors.
Table status columns should use a domain adapter and canonical StatusBadge.
Current status and historical event outcomes remain distinct.
Raw integration, tenant, and account status codes must be normalized.
Recommendation, review, and final decision statuses must not be conflated.

prohibited: Inferring success from optimistic local state.

notes: The owning entity or feature supplies a normalized tone, localized label, and optional context.

responsive.strategy: Remain compact while allowing localized labels to wrap only when necessary.
responsive.compact: Use compact size and controlled wrapping. The badge must not force a table or header to overflow.
responsive.ultrawide: Do not scale with available viewport width.
responsive.overflowPolicy: Labels may wrap to a second line when required. Long explanations use another component.
responsive.zoomExpectation: Must remain legible at 200% text scaling without relying on color or animation.

accessibility.semanticElement: span or appropriate static status text; dynamic changes may be wrapped by a status region
accessibility.accessibleName: Visible status label with optional additional context.
keyboard: Static status badges are not focusable.
Supplementary tooltip triggers are keyboard accessible only when actual supplementary context exists.
focus: StatusBadge does not alter focus order.
announcements: Material dynamic status changes may be announced by the owning workflow.
Frequent processing updates should not produce excessive announcements.
Static statuses are not live regions by default.
aria: Avoid unnecessary status or alert roles for static labels.
Decorative icons are hidden from assistive technology.
Animated processing icons expose equivalent textual status.
accessibility.colorIndependence: Every status includes a visible textual label and may include a semantic icon in addition to color.

content.typical: A concise one-to-three-word status with an optional icon.
content.maximum: A short phrase. Detailed consequences or recovery instructions require InlineAlert, ErrorState, PermissionState, ProcessingState, or StaleDataNotice.
content.wrapping: Prefer one line; allow controlled wrapping for localization.
content.truncation: Do not truncate when the remaining label becomes ambiguous.
content.localization: All labels and supplementary context support localization.
content.emptyBehavior: A status without a label does not render.
content.technicalContent: Raw enum keys, status integers, machine-state codes, and internal workflow IDs are prohibited.

notes: Each domain should define an adapter from its raw status model into the canonical StatusBadge contract.
Feature adapters must not introduce additional arbitrary visual tones.

Timeline.name: Timeline
Timeline.description: Canonical chronological or reverse-chronological history for activity, workflow transitions, audit events, decisions, and domain milestones.
capabilities: Present ordered events with actor, time, status, description, and supporting metadata.
Distinguish ordinary activity, workflow transition, decision history, and audit history.
Group or progressively disclose bounded event details.
Communicate event ordering, source, and current state accessibly.
Support loading, empty, error, restricted, and paginated history states.

foundation.source: Native ordered-list semantics, Stack, MetadataList, StatusBadge, DefinitionList, disclosure foundation
foundation.reason: Temporal history requires explicit event anatomy, ordering, disclosure, status mapping, accessible timestamps, bounded detail, and scope-aware states.

activity.intent: Present user-relevant activity and domain events.
prohibitedUse: Complex state machine without explicit transition labels.

workflow.intent: Present meaningful state transitions and milestones in a user workflow.

decision.intent: Present human or policy decisions with actor, rationale, evidence context, and resulting status.
prohibitedUse: Machine recommendation presented as a final human decision.
Decision event without actor or authoritative source.

audit.intent: Present authorized audit events with stable identity, actor, timestamp, action, scope, and safe diagnostic context.

compact.intent: Dense history with concise event content.

default.intent: Ordinary event history with supporting metadata and optional details.

slots.name: heading
slots.description: Optional visible history heading.
contentRestrictions: Use when the containing section does not already identify the history.

slots.name: summary
slots.description: Optional event-count, active-filter, scope, or freshness summary.
contentRestrictions: Do not duplicate the complete event list.
Unknown totals remain unknown.

slots.name: event
slots.description: One ordered historical event.
contentRestrictions: Every event requires stable identity and authoritative timestamp.
The event must describe a user-meaningful action or transition.

slots.name: marker
slots.description: Visual marker representing event type or status.
contentRestrictions: Marker meaning must also be present in text or status.
Decorative timeline lines are hidden from assistive technology.

slots.name: title
slots.description: Concise event action or transition label.
contentRestrictions: Use active user-facing language.
Do not display raw event codes.

slots.name: timestamp
slots.description: Authoritative localized event date and time.
contentRestrictions: Include timezone context according to project policy.
Relative time alone is insufficient for audit events.

slots.name: actor
slots.description: Optional human, system, integration, or policy actor.
contentRestrictions: Distinguish human, system, integration, and automated-policy actors.
Do not invent a human actor for automated events.

slots.name: status
slots.description: Optional resulting or current event status.
contentRestrictions: Status refers to the event or resulting transition, not necessarily the current entity state.

slots.name: description
slots.description: Optional concise explanation, rationale, or outcome.
contentRestrictions: Decision rationale must not be truncated into ambiguity.
Raw logs and transport messages are prohibited.

slots.name: metadata
slots.description: Optional supporting source, scope, version, correlation, or related-entity context.
contentRestrictions: Technical metadata is restricted to approved administrative or audit use.
Secrets and tokens are prohibited.

slots.name: details
slots.description: Optional progressively disclosed bounded event details.
contentRestrictions: Details remain bounded.
Do not render complete raw event payloads.
Material decision rationale should not be hidden by default.

slots.name: actions
slots.description: Optional event-specific actions such as opening the source, comparing changes, or copying an approved reference.
contentRestrictions: Actions remain low frequency and event-specific.
Do not place destructive entity actions inside historical events.

slots.name: state
slots.description: Loading, empty, error, permission, or unavailable history state.
contentRestrictions: Use the smallest truthful scope.
Existing events remain visible during background refresh.

slots.name: pagination
slots.description: Optional bounded history pagination or load-more navigation.
contentRestrictions: The pagination model must match the backend history contract.
Do not append unbounded history indefinitely without virtualization or pagination policy.

props.name: variant
props.description: Semantic event-history type.
restrictions: Audit variant requires explicit capability and safe diagnostic policy.
Decision variant requires an authoritative decision source.

props.name: size
props.description: Approved history density.
restrictions: Compact must not remove required event context.

props.name: order
props.description: Visible event order.
restrictions: The order must be stated or visually clear.
Audit and activity histories normally show newest first unless workflow progression requires ascending order.

props.name: expandedItems
props.description: Controlled identifiers of events whose optional details are expanded.
restrictions: Only events with bounded optional details may expand.

props.name: onExpandedItemsChange
props.description: Controlled disclosure-state callback.
restrictions: The component does not fetch event details automatically unless an approved feature adapter owns that behavior.

props.name: loading
props.description: Indicates initial history loading.
restrictions: Background refresh preserves existing events.

props.name: refreshing
props.description: Indicates background history synchronization.
restrictions: Refreshing must not reset expansion or focus.

spacingOwnership: Timeline owns spacing and connective structure among events.
TimelineEvent owns spacing among title, timestamp, actor, status, description, metadata, details, and actions.
The containing section owns spacing around the complete timeline.
composition.surfaceOwnership: Timeline owns no required outer card. Individual event surfaces remain subtle and are used only when the variant requires stronger grouping.
rules: Events are ordered by authoritative timestamps.
Historical event status is distinct from current entity status.
Relative time is supplemented by absolute time where auditability matters.
Raw event payloads are never rendered directly.
Expansion and pagination remain bounded.
System, integration, policy, and human actors remain distinguishable.

recipeCompatibility.notes: Use for activity, workflow, and audit history.
Audit history requires explicit capability and safe content mapping.
Use decision variant for prior human decisions and audit variant for system events.
Use only for a bounded recent-activity summary, with navigation to full history.
Use for selected-record preview history.

notes: Event data, pagination, filtering, and permission state remain outside the component.
Optional event-detail expansion may be controlled by the owning feature.
Timeline manages disclosure focus behavior.
Navigation, copy, comparison, and event-source actions are supplied externally.

responsive.strategy: Preserve event order, title, timestamp, actor, and status while stacking optional metadata and details.
responsive.compact: Use compact marker spacing, stack event header content, and move low-frequency actions to overflow.
responsive.medium: Allow title, actor, status, and timestamp to wrap across two rows.
responsive.wide: Use the approved event anatomy with metadata and optional details aligned clearly.
responsive.ultrawide: Constrain event reading width rather than stretching descriptions across the route.
responsive.overflowPolicy: Event text and metadata wrap. Technical references use approved safe copy or truncation behavior.
responsive.zoomExpectation: Event headers stack before actor, status, timestamp, or actions become difficult to associate at 125% browser zoom.

accessibility.semanticElement: ordered list containing independently structured event list items
accessibility.accessibleName: Visible history heading or accessible label provided by the containing section.
keyboard: Event actions and pagination are keyboard operable.
Static event content is not unnecessarily focusable.
focus: DOM order follows visible chronological order.
Collapsed details restore focus to their disclosure trigger.
Background refresh preserves focus and expanded state.
announcements: Newly loaded event batches may be announced politely when user initiated.
Routine background refresh does not announce every new event.
Dynamic workflow status changes use the owning status or feedback policy.
aria: Use time elements with machine-readable datetime values.
Disclosure controls use aria-expanded and appropriate relationships.
Decorative timeline lines and markers are hidden from assistive technology.
accessibility.colorIndependence: Event status, actor type, current milestone, changes, and failures use text, semantics, icons, or shape in addition to color.

content.minimum: One event with title and authoritative timestamp.
content.typical: Event title, timestamp, actor, status, concise description, and supporting metadata.
content.maximum: A bounded paginated history. Raw logs and unlimited events require another authorized diagnostic system.
content.wrapping: Titles, descriptions, actor names, statuses, metadata, and actions wrap naturally.
content.truncation: Decision rationale and material outcomes must not be truncated into ambiguity. Secondary identifiers may truncate with full-value access.
content.localization: Support localized dates, times, actor labels, statuses, actions, and event descriptions.
content.emptyBehavior: No historical events use an explicit EmptyState rather than a blank region.
content.technicalContent: Safe technical references are allowed only in authorized audit contexts. Raw payloads, tokens, secrets, stack traces, and internal event codes are prohibited.

notes: Feature-level event adapters map raw domain and audit events into the canonical TimelineEvent contract.
Timeline is not a log viewer.

FreshnessIndicator.name: FreshnessIndicator
FreshnessIndicator.description: Canonical presentation of when data was calculated, synchronized, observed, or refreshed, including normalized freshness state and absolute time context.
capabilities: Communicate when data was last updated or calculated.
Distinguish fresh, aging, stale, and unknown freshness states.
Present relative and absolute time without hiding timezone context.
Expose an optional refresh action or data-source explanation.
Prevent stale data from appearing indistinguishable from current data.

foundation.source: HTML time element, MetadataList, StatusBadge, Tooltip, Button
foundation.reason: Freshness communication requires localized relative and absolute time, explicit status normalization, timezone policy, stale distinction, and controlled refresh behavior.

fresh.intent: Communicate that the data is within the approved freshness threshold.
prohibitedUse: The freshness threshold has been exceeded.

aging.intent: Communicate that the data remains usable but is approaching its freshness threshold.
allowedUse: Dashboard data approaching its recency target.
Cached data still valid but no longer recent.
prohibitedUse: Data is already outside the allowed threshold.

stale.intent: Communicate that the data is outside the approved freshness threshold or has been superseded.
allowedUse: Dashboard data outside the recency threshold.

unknown.intent: Communicate that the data timestamp or freshness state is not available.

compact.intent: Short freshness context inside metadata, metrics, and table footers.

default.intent: Prominent freshness context inside an analytical or stale-data region.

slots.name: icon
slots.description: Optional semantic freshness or synchronization icon.
contentRestrictions: The icon is not the only source of meaning.
Rotation or animation is reserved for active refreshing and respects reduced motion.

slots.name: relativeTime
slots.description: Concise localized relative freshness label.
contentRestrictions: Examples include Atualizado há 5 minutos or Calculado há 2 horas.
Relative time must not be the only timestamp in audit-sensitive contexts.

slots.name: absoluteTime
slots.description: Localized absolute timestamp including approved timezone context.
contentRestrictions: Required for audit-sensitive and review-sensitive contexts.
The machine-readable datetime value must use an unambiguous format.

slots.name: status
slots.description: Optional explicit freshness-state label.
contentRestrictions: Required when aging, stale, or unknown state would not otherwise be clear.

slots.name: source
slots.description: Optional concise data-source or calculation-source context.
contentRestrictions: Use user-facing source names.
Do not expose endpoint names or internal service identifiers.

slots.name: action
slots.description: Optional refresh, retry, or source-details action.
contentRestrictions: Refresh is shown only when the user can initiate it.
The action must not imply guaranteed freshness before completion.

props.name: status
props.description: Normalized freshness state resolved by the owning data policy.
restrictions: The component does not calculate product freshness thresholds.
The owning feature or data layer resolves this state.

props.name: size
props.description: Approved freshness presentation scale.
restrictions: Compact must not omit required stale or unknown meaning.

props.name: dateTime
props.description: Machine-readable authoritative timestamp.
restrictions: Use an unambiguous ISO-compatible value.
Missing timestamp requires unknown state.

props.name: relativeLabel
props.description: Localized relative-time label supplied by an approved date-time formatter.
restrictions: Must not expose raw ISO strings.
Must remain consistent with dateTime.

props.name: absoluteLabel
props.description: Localized absolute date-time label including approved timezone context.
restrictions: Required when precise time affects review, audit, or decision quality.

props.name: refreshing
props.description: Indicates that a manual or automatic refresh is currently running.
restrictions: Refreshing does not automatically change status to fresh.
Fresh status is applied only after authoritative completion.

prohibitedParents: Button when freshness is only decorative
spacingOwnership: FreshnessIndicator owns spacing among icon, relative time, absolute time, state, source, and action.
The containing component owns spacing around the complete indicator.
composition.surfaceOwnership: FreshnessIndicator owns no surface in compact mode. Stale treatment may use a compact semantic surface when required.
rules: Freshness state is resolved outside the component.
Unknown freshness is never treated as fresh.
Relative labels are supplemented by precise time when decisions or audit require it.
Refreshing and fresh are distinct.
Blocking conflicts use StaleDataNotice rather than FreshnessIndicator alone.

recipeCompatibility.notes: Dashboard scope and metrics must communicate data recency when not real-time.
Use for collection synchronization context and background-refresh status.
Use when entity or related data may lag behind the authoritative source.
Integration, synchronization, and diagnostic states require precise timestamp context.
Evidence, recommendation, and decision freshness materially affect review validity.

notes: The owning feature supplies authoritative timestamps, normalized freshness state, localized labels, source context, and optional actions.
Refresh, retry, and source-detail actions are supplied externally.

responsive.strategy: Preserve freshness state and precise time context while wrapping source and action content.
responsive.compact: Show concise relative time and explicit stale or unknown state. Precise time may remain in an accessible tooltip when the context is not audit-sensitive.
responsive.medium: Show relative time, optional absolute time, and source context.
responsive.wide: Allow inline relative time, absolute time, source, and refresh action.
responsive.ultrawide: Remain compact and aligned to the owning component.
responsive.overflowPolicy: Date, timezone, source, and actions wrap. Raw timestamps are not displayed.
responsive.zoomExpectation: The indicator wraps before freshness meaning or actions become unreadable at 125% browser zoom.

accessibility.semanticElement: time element combined with static status text; active refresh may use a status region
accessibility.accessibleName: Visible freshness label and precise time context.
keyboard: Static freshness content is not focusable.
Tooltip, refresh, retry, and source actions are keyboard operable.
focus: Background refresh does not move or reset focus.
Optional tooltip and actions follow logical DOM order.
announcements: User-initiated refresh completion may be announced politely.
Routine automatic freshness updates are not repeatedly announced.
New stale or unknown state may be announced when it materially changes user decisions.
aria: Use a machine-readable datetime value on time elements.
Decorative icons are hidden from assistive technology.
Active refresh must not rely only on icon animation.
accessibility.colorIndependence: Fresh, aging, stale, unknown, and refreshing states use text, precise time, semantics, or icons in addition to color.

content.minimum: One freshness state and a timestamp or explicit unknown-freshness label.
content.typical: Relative time, precise timestamp, normalized state, and optional data source.
content.maximum: Concise recency context. Full synchronization diagnostics belong in an authorized diagnostic region.
content.wrapping: Relative time, absolute time, source, state, and actions wrap naturally.
content.truncation: Do not truncate stale or unknown meaning. Long source names may truncate only when full value remains accessible.
content.localization: Support locale-specific date, time, timezone, pluralization, and relative-time formatting.
content.emptyBehavior: Missing timestamp requires an explicit unknown state rather than an empty indicator.
content.technicalContent: Raw ISO timestamps, cache keys, query timestamps, endpoint names, and synchronization payloads are prohibited in ordinary presentation.

notes: The product data policy determines freshness thresholds.
An approved date-time utility formats relative and absolute labels before they reach the component.

checks.description: The analytical data-display catalog must validate against the component catalog schema.
checks.remediation: Correct invalid or missing component catalog fields.

checks.description: Analytical component IDs, names, implementations, public imports, and canonical responsibilities must remain unique.
checks.remediation: Resolve duplicate ownership or merge overlapping analytical components.

checks.description: Shared analytical components must not execute queries, calculate domain metrics, map raw statuses, evaluate permissions, or apply product freshness thresholds.
checks.remediation: Move domain calculation, mapping, data access, capability evaluation, and freshness policy to the owning entity, feature, or route.

checks.description: Metric hierarchy must identify dominant, supporting, attention, comparison, and progress roles rather than applying equal visual treatment by default.
checks.remediation: Correct the screen contract, MetricGroup variant, and MetricCard priority assignments.

checks.description: Trend direction and trend meaning must remain separate, and movement must not be treated as success or failure without domain interpretation.
checks.remediation: Provide an explicit feature-owned trend interpretation.

checks.description: Raw backend statuses, event codes, timestamps, metric keys, and freshness policy details must not be rendered directly.
checks.remediation: Map technical values through approved domain adapters, localization utilities, and canonical analytical components.

checks.description: Status, metric, timeline, and freshness meaning must remain perceivable without depending only on color, animation, or iconography.
checks.remediation: Correct labels, semantics, accessible names, reduced-motion behavior, or color-independent content.

checks.description: Analytical components must preserve hierarchy, event ordering, status meaning, and freshness context without page-level horizontal overflow at approved viewports and zoom levels.
checks.remediation: Correct responsive hierarchy, wrapping, container width, event composition, or action placement.

checks.description: Page-local KPI cards, metric grids, status pills, activity lists, audit timelines, and freshness labels similar to canonical components require review.
checks.remediation: Reuse the canonical analytical component or document why the local implementation is semantically distinct.
